title: Agent architectural review and ground-up rebuild

completion_criteria.text: Current-state audit complete: every gap in the roster, the agent definitions and the observation machinery identified with measured evidence from the ledger and the definition files.
Audit delivered in a form the user can read and navigate - a self-contained HTML explainer with diagrams, written for a reader with no prior domain knowledge.
Target architecture designed and approved by the user: roster shape, tool grants, who may delegate, and how the configuration observes itself.
Agent and observer teardown and rebuild executed without breaking the live coupling surface: rules and skills naming agents by string, 405 worktree copies, four backup profiles, derived residuals.
New configuration verified in real use: dispatch routes to the intended agents, and the observation system attributes every run and records an outcome.

spine.active_goal: Get the target architecture to explicit user approval so c3 can close, then execute the teardown and rebuild at c4.
spine.next_step: WAIT for the user's SPECIFIC instructions. Do NOT auto-proceed, and do NOT edit any agent, rule, hook or skill file. The round-3/3b report is delivered at ~/.agent/diagrams/agent-roster-rebuild-recommendations.html (248 KB): 15 decisions settled in section 13, 6 items open in section 14, and 3 of the report's own claims corrected in place in section 09. The validator that gated edits to that file lived in this session's scratchpad and is gone - rebuild it before splicing that file again.
spine.last_session: Amended the report through rounds 3 and 3b: seven investigations, seventeen fragments spliced, three of the report's own claims corrected, two unclearable gates fixed. Validator passed at exit 0.

open_risks.text: Never read `emitter` in the events log as a measurement — it is a hardcoded constant on every row, and treating it as signal already produced one wrong conclusion
Archive the events log before any teardown step — 8.7 MB across 46 days is the only artifact here that cannot be regenerated, and it is the baseline a new roster gets measured against
Repoint the five skills that name deleted agents — verification-discipline and report break outright, since every branch of their logic invokes verification-strategist and report-writer by name
Land the new mitosis engine before starting the rebuild — this work targets that engine, whose dispatch table comes from engine source literals rather than a static allowlist

Declare StructuredOutput in tools: on all 13 agents before the rebuild lands — the engine's census gate fails if any dispatchable agent omits it, all 15 current agents omit it today, and the lint that would catch it is NOT on the main branch
Decide whether this thread supersedes the paused thread agent-roster-gap-resolution — it covers overlapping ground against an older SPEC and was not touched in rounds 2 or 3

Ask the user which telemetry figure measures what before citing either — the report uses 15,301 and 15,573 for the same corpus, and round 3 propagated 15,573 more widely, so the inconsistency is now more visible

Define what a browser-based reproduction must RETURN before the rebuild grants investigator browser tools — a screenshot is an observation, not a re-runnable receipt, and the report grants the tools without settling this
Choose the replacement name for release-engineer — decision 15 settles THAT it is renamed, not what to; candidates so far are branch-steward and integration-engineer

key_decisions.title: The audit pass characterises the current state and recommends nothing
Replace all 56 agents with 13 in four bands, with the dispatch tool held only by the Opus leads
Terminate review loops by closing the reviewer's question, not by capping rounds or turns
Rebuild the observer to append one line per run and do everything else at audit time
Put load-bearing rules in agent bodies, generated from shared fragments with a drift check
User rulings on the six open rebuild questions, and the addition of the observer to this thread
Always reproduce a bug before diagnosing it, and test the fix for cause rather than effect
Skills reach agents only by preload, and the dispatch tool goes to Leads only
Withdraw the report skill and put the answer-format standard in every agent body
Keep the code-reviewer agent, adopt receiving-code-review, drop requesting-code-review
Keep release-engineer broad; the real problem is per-duty procedure loading
The zero-compliance measurement was an instrumentation artifact; re-ground the channel thesis on documentation

out_of_scope: Mutating any agent, rule, hook or skill file until the target architecture at c3 is approved.

Restoring the bash gate's ask verdict so that 'destructive operations require explicit confirmation' becomes enforceable - that is a decision about the gate, not about agents, and it is filed in report section 14.
Cutting the ~13,300-token standing instruction load carried on every dispatch - a cut changes behaviour and nothing yet measures which rules are load-bearing.
